newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan seeks 40 pct share of Japan minivan market.
newsitem.headline: Nissan seeks 40 pct share of Japan minivan market.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd launched a new model of large minivan on Monday and said it hoped that the latest addition to its line-up would help boost its market share in this sector to 40 percent.
Nissan currently holds 10 percent of Japan's market for large, multi-purpose minivans.
"Ten percent is too low. We want to boost this to 40 percent," Nissan president Yoshikazu Hanawa told reporters at the launch of the firm's new Caravan/Homy Elgrand.
Nissan, Japan's second biggest carmaker, launched the new model with a monthly sales target of 5,000 units.
Japanese demand for large minivans stands at about 10,000 units per month, a Nissan spokesman said.
Hanawa said Nissan launched the Elgrand to try to catch up with other manufacturers in the sector and would also launch compact minivans next year.
The Elgrand features a luxury interior and a bigger engine than its competitors, Hanawa said.
The Elgrand's list price will start at 2.655 million yen for a two-wheel-drive version and 2.955 million yen for a four-wheel-drive version.

"The selling price is 200,000 yen cheaper than that of competitors such as Toyota's Estima (called the Previa overseas) and the Granvia," Tadao Takei, a vice president in charge of domestic sales, said.
